questions.q: What is a red ocean, according to the summary?
a: A crowded market where firms fight over existing demand
An untapped market with almost no competitors
A market created by a single new regulation
A market where one company holds a monopoly
questions.why: The red ocean is the battlefield where businesses compete for the same customers.

questions.q: Why does the summary call the blue ocean more attractive?
a: It is untapped, so a company can innovate instead of fight
It guarantees profits with little investment
It has fewer government regulations
It attracts customers who dislike new products
questions.why: In the blue ocean, innovation is the main focus rather than beating rivals.

questions.q: Which four questions make up the strategy canvas?
a: Eliminate, reduce, raise and create industry factors
Analyze, compare, imitate and improve competitors
Segment, target, position and promote products
Plan, build, measure and scale operations
questions.why: The canvas asks what to remove, lower, lift above standard, and invent.

questions.q: What did low-cost airlines eliminate to reshape the industry?
a: Airport lounges, while adding more frequent flights
Checked baggage, while lowering ticket prices
Online booking, while opening ticket counters
Assigned seating, while adding premium cabins
questions.why: The summary uses this as an example of removing what customers did not value.

questions.q: What does value innovation mean in the summary?
a: Creating a leap in value that opens new market space
Cutting prices until rivals cannot compete
Adding features to match every competitor
Improving existing products in small steps
questions.why: Value innovation is the cornerstone of reaching the blue ocean.
